title: Massachusetts Pharmacy Internship: Hours, Supervision, and the Examination Bar
topic: Pharmacy personnel / Massachusetts pharmacy interns under 247 CMR 8.01
subtopic: Internship credit and its composition, direct preceptor supervision and its limits, the entry route each class of graduate must clear, and the conduct that bars examination
learning_objectives: State the internship hour requirement with its internal 1000-hour and 500-hour composition, and name the alternative experiential pathway that reaches the same 1500-hour total.

Apply the daily credit ceiling, keep it apart from the separate limit on hours of practice in any 24-hour period, and distinguish time spent at a site from hours creditable toward the internship requirement.
Identify who may directly supervise a pharmacy intern, how many interns one preceptor may supervise at one time, and what a supervised intern may in turn supervise.
Trace the entry route for a domestic graduate, a PharmD graduate entering a Massachusetts residency, and a graduate of a non-approved college or school of pharmacy.
Name who decides whether a school programme or out-of-state experience counts toward the internship, and on what submission.
State the reporting duties that sit on the intern personally and the consequence the regulation attaches to intern misconduct.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts pharmacy internship is the supervised practice a candidate must have completed before the Commonwealth will license that candidate as a pharmacist, and 247 CMR 8.01(1) states the requirement in hours rather than in years or job titles. The first pathway is at least 1500 hours of Board-approved pharmacy internship experience, and those 1500 hours are not undifferentiated: at least 1000 of them must be acquired in a pharmacy or pharmacy-related setting approved by the Board, and at least 500 in any one, or any combination, of Board-approved internships in clinical pharmacy, a demonstration project, manufacturing, or analytical or industrial pharmacy. The second pathway reaches the same total by a different route, at least 1500 intern hours acquired through experiential pharmacy education, and it is available where the student is a graduate of an ACPE-accredited college or university. Reading 1500 as a single undivided number is the most common way to misstate this requirement.

Supervision is the spine of the whole area. 247 CMR 8.01(3) provides that a pharmacy intern shall work under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor, and both halves of that phrase are defined terms. Under 247 CMR 2.00 a preceptor is a registered pharmacist in good standing who has completed at least one year of the actual practice of pharmacy and whom the Board has approved to supervise and direct the training of pharmacy interns, so a pharmacist with less than a year of actual practice, one who is not in good standing, or one the Board has not approved is not a preceptor, however willing. Direct supervision of an intern is the supervision a Board-approved registered pharmacist preceptor gives by overseeing and directing the intern's professional activities, and it includes directly reviewing the intern's work, so being in the building is not the whole of it. The same definitions let a pharmacy intern engage in the full range of activities conducted by a registered pharmacist, provided that at all times the intern is under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor. The requirement carries no hours trigger, so accumulated experience does not convert itself into an authority to work alone; an intern who has logged 1400 hours stands in the same supervisory position as one who has logged 40. The obligation is written on the intern, but it describes a relationship, and the preceptor side of that relationship carries its own limit: under 247 CMR 8.01(16) a registered pharmacist preceptor shall not directly supervise more than two pharmacy interns at one time. That cap counts interns and stands independently of the general support-personnel supervisory ratio in 247 CMR 8.06(3), so headroom under one limit does not create headroom under the other. Within the supervised relationship the intern is not merely passive: 247 CMR 8.01(15) allows a pharmacy intern acting under the direct supervision of a registered preceptor to supervise pharmacy technicians, and the intern's own supervised status is the condition of that authority rather than an obstacle to it.

Hours are earned day by day, and two different 12-hour limits bear on the day. The first is a limit on credit: 247 CMR 8.01(4) provides that a pharmacy intern may not receive more than 12 hours of pharmacy internship credit per day, which makes the record of creditable hours a different document from the record of time spent at a site. The second is a limit on practice itself, and it sits in 247 CMR 9.01(17): a pharmacist, pharmacy intern, or pharmacy technician may not practice in a pharmacy for more than 12 hours in a 24 hour period without completing an eight consecutive hour rest period prior to resuming work in a pharmacy. Only an extenuating circumstance lets the intern exceed 12 hours, in order to act in the best interest of the patient, and then only if the time in excess of 12 hours is minimized and the licensee documents the extenuating circumstance. The practice limit counts time practising in a pharmacy, not every hour spent on the premises. A long intern shift is therefore a practice question before it is a credit question, and even excess time worked lawfully under that exception does not lift the day's credit above 12 hours. Which hours count is also not left to the site or the school. Under 247 CMR 8.01(12) Massachusetts approved colleges and schools of pharmacy shall submit to the Board a written description of each demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program for which pharmacy internship credit is desired, and the Board may determine whether student participation in those projects or programs may be credited to the internship requirement: the school proposes and the Board decides. The Board in turn issues, under 247 CMR 8.01(13), a Summary of Objectives and Procedures for Pharmacy Internship together with guidelines for registered pharmacist preceptors and pharmacy interns. Experience acquired elsewhere is not simply lost either: 247 CMR 8.01(11) allows the Board to grant credit for out-of-state pharmacy internship experience where an affidavit or certificate of approval issued by the jurisdiction in which the experience was acquired is presented to the Board indicating that the experience was duly approved there.

Three different candidates arrive at a Massachusetts internship through three different doors, and the door determines what must be in place first. A pharmacy intern who graduates from an approved college or school of pharmacy needs nothing new in order to keep working: 247 CMR 8.01(10) provides that a pharmacy intern who has graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy may continue to act in the capacity of pharmacy intern until he or she becomes licensed as a pharmacist, so graduation closes the degree programme and not the intern capacity. The provision continues a capacity the graduate already holds as an intern; it does not make a graduate who never held one an intern. A PharmD graduate of an approved school who has accepted a residency in Massachusetts is treated more strictly, because a residency appointment is a position and not a credential: under 247 CMR 8.01(8) that graduate shall apply for and obtain a pharmacy intern license until such time as he or she obtains a Massachusetts pharmacist license, and a PharmD graduate enrolled in a residency in Massachusetts shall either hold a Massachusetts pharmacist license or hold a Massachusetts pharmacy intern license and be supervised by a pharmacist. A graduate of a non-approved college or school of pharmacy faces a gate that closes before the internship begins at all: 247 CMR 8.01(7) requires that, before the commencement of a pharmacy internship in Massachusetts, that graduate have authorization from NABP to sit for the FPGEE issued within the preceding year, and provide a copy of that authorization to the Board along with any other documentation the Board requires. The currency window is the element candidates drop: an authorization that exists is not the same as an authorization issued within the preceding year, and an FPGEE authorization is not an FPGEC certification.

The last layer is reporting and conduct, and it is the layer on which an internship can cost a candidate the examination rather than merely a placement. Under 247 CMR 8.01(9), during the course of the pharmacy internship, preceptors and pharmacy interns shall in a timely manner submit, on a form provided by the Board, such information as the Board may require regarding the internship, so the duty to keep the Board informed runs throughout the internship and on both sides of the supervisory relationship. Under 247 CMR 8.01(18) a pharmacy intern shall provide written notification to the Board within 14 days of his or her withdrawal from an approved college or school of pharmacy or PharmD program; that duty is the intern's own rather than the school's or the employer's, it is triggered by the withdrawal itself and not by any later decision about returning, and it is the mirror image of 8.01(10), where graduation triggers no notification at all. Most seriously, 247 CMR 8.01(17) provides that a pharmacy intern found to have engaged in conduct in violation of federal and/or state laws and/or regulations may be prohibited from taking the examination for licensure, in addition to other sanctions imposed by the Board. The two phrases worth holding on to are 'may be prohibited' and 'in addition to': the examination bar is discretionary rather than automatic, and it sits on top of whatever the Board does about the intern license rather than in place of it. One limit on the licensure consequences of conduct sits in the same chapter: under 247 CMR 8.08 no person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline, or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, so long as the services provided would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts, and 247 CMR 3.05 says the same for licensure as a pharmacist.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy intern works a scheduled 12-hour Saturday shift at a Board-approved community pharmacy under a registered pharmacist preceptor who oversees and reviews the intern's work throughout. As the shift ends, a patient arrives from a hospital discharge needing a medication that cannot wait, and the intern stays a further 90 minutes, no longer than the prescription takes; the intern and the preceptor, who works the same hours, each write a note recording why. The preceptor proposes signing the internship log for all 13.5 hours, and the manager proposes scheduling the same 13.5-hour Saturday every week. What does the law make of the day, and of the proposal?
steps: Take the practice limit first. 247 CMR 9.01(17) provides that a pharmacy intern may not practice in a pharmacy for more than 12 hours in a 24 hour period without completing an eight consecutive hour rest period prior to resuming work in a pharmacy, so the extra 90 minutes needs the provision's exception.

Test the exception on these facts. An extenuating circumstance allows the intern to exceed 12 hours in order to act in the best interest of the patient, provided the time in excess of 12 hours is minimized and the licensee documents the extenuating circumstance; an urgent discharge prescription, an overrun kept to the time it needed and each licensee's own written note meet each element, for the intern and equally for the preceptor, whom the same provision binds.

Apply the credit ceiling separately. 247 CMR 8.01(4) provides that a pharmacy intern may not receive more than 12 hours of pharmacy internship credit per day, so the day yields 12 creditable hours whatever the lawful reason for the overrun, and the preceptor's signature does not raise the ceiling.

Turn to the standing proposal. A 13.5-hour shift scheduled every week has no extenuating circumstance behind it, so it is practice beyond 12 hours in a 24 hour period that 247 CMR 9.01(17) does not allow, and conduct in violation of state regulations is what 247 CMR 8.01(17) lets the Board answer with a bar on the licensure examination.

Close out the day. Before resuming work in a pharmacy the intern must complete an eight consecutive hour rest period, and for every hour worked, credited or not, 247 CMR 8.01(3) requires direct supervision by a registered pharmacist preceptor.
worked_examples.resolution: Twelve hours of internship credit for the day. The 90-minute overrun was lawful only because it met the extenuating-circumstance exception in 247 CMR 9.01(17), and the weekly 13.5-hour schedule must be refused outright. The error the scenario invites is treating a long intern shift as a question about the log, when the practice limit decides whether the time may be worked at all and the credit ceiling then caps what counts.

worked_examples.scenario: A graduate of a non-approved school of pharmacy overseas has moved to Massachusetts and has arranged an internship placement starting in two weeks. He holds NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE that was issued twenty months ago and has not been renewed. The placement site is willing to start him immediately under a registered pharmacist preceptor. May the internship commence?
steps: Identify the class of candidate. He is a graduate of a non-approved college or school of pharmacy, so 247 CMR 8.01(7) applies before anything else.

Read the gate as a precondition. 8.01(7) speaks to what must be true 'before the commencement of a pharmacy internship in Massachusetts', so a willing site and an available preceptor do not move the sequence.
Test the currency of the credential. The authorization must have been issued within the preceding year; one issued twenty months ago falls outside that window and does not satisfy the provision.
Check the filing element too. A qualifying authorization must be copied to the Board along with any other documentation the Board requires, so holding it privately is not enough.
worked_examples.resolution: No. The internship may not commence on a twenty-month-old authorization, and the error the scenario invites is reading 8.01(7) as satisfied by the mere existence of an FPGEE authorization rather than by one issued within the preceding year and provided to the Board.

worked_examples.scenario: On a busy evening a registered pharmacist preceptor is already directly supervising two pharmacy interns. The manager asks the preceptor to take a third intern for the shift, pointing out that the pharmacy sits comfortably under its overall support-personnel ratio, and suggests that one of the existing interns could instead be counted as supervising the two technicians on duty. Is either arrangement available?
steps: Take the preceptor cap first. 247 CMR 8.01(16) provides that a registered pharmacist preceptor shall not directly supervise more than two pharmacy interns at one time, so the third intern cannot be added to this preceptor.

Refuse the ratio argument. The 8.01(16) cap counts interns per preceptor and is independent of the general support-personnel supervisory ratio in 247 CMR 8.06(3); slack in one does not create slack in the other.
Now test the second suggestion. 247 CMR 8.01(15) does allow a pharmacy intern to supervise pharmacy technicians, so overseeing the two technicians is permitted in itself.

Read the condition attached to it. The intern may do so only while acting under the direct supervision of a registered preceptor, so the arrangement does not free the intern from 8.01(3) and does not reduce the preceptor's own load.
worked_examples.resolution: The third intern must be declined, while the intern overseeing technicians is permissible. The error the scenario invites is treating the overall support-personnel ratio as the only supervision limit, and treating an intern who supervises technicians as having stepped out of the direct supervision that 8.01(15) makes a condition of that very authority.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy intern withdraws from her PharmD program at the end of a semester, intending to reapply the following year, and keeps working her usual shifts. During the same period the Board finds that she dispensed without the preceptor present on several occasions. She assumes the school will tell the Board about the withdrawal and that the worst outcome of the finding is a sanction on her intern license. Advise her.
steps: Locate the notification duty. 247 CMR 8.01(18) puts written notification of withdrawal from an approved college or school of pharmacy or PharmD program on the intern personally, within 14 days of the withdrawal.
Reject the two deferrals she is relying on. The duty is not discharged by the school and does not wait on her decision about reapplying; it is triggered by the withdrawal itself.

Distinguish the graduation case she may be thinking of. Under 247 CMR 8.01(10) a pharmacy intern who has graduated from an approved college or school may continue acting as a pharmacy intern until licensed, and graduation triggers no notification, which is why withdrawal and graduation must not be run together.

Read the conduct consequence. 247 CMR 8.01(17) provides that an intern found to have engaged in conduct in violation of federal and/or state laws and/or regulations may be prohibited from taking the examination for licensure, in addition to other sanctions imposed by the Board.

Add the reporting obligation that runs alongside. Under 247 CMR 8.01(9), during the course of the internship, preceptors and interns must in a timely manner submit, on a Board form, such information about the internship as the Board requires.
worked_examples.resolution: She owes the Board written notice within 14 days herself, and the finding can reach further than her intern license. The error the scenario invites is reading the examination bar in 8.01(17) as an alternative to other sanctions, when the provision makes it an additional one, and reading the withdrawal notice as somebody else's filing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacy intern may not receive more than ______ hours of pharmacy internship credit per ______.
Two 12-hour limits apply to a Massachusetts pharmacy intern. What does each one measure?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 247 CMR 8.01(4) caps internship credit at 12 hours per day. 247 CMR 9.01(17) limits practice in a pharmacy to 12 hours in a 24 hour period without an eight consecutive hour rest period before resuming work, and allows more only in an extenuating circumstance, in the best interest of the patient, with the excess minimized and the circumstance documented by the licensee.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: On the first pathway the internship is at least ______ hours in total, of which at least ______ hours in a pharmacy or pharmacy-related setting approved by the Board and at least ______ hours in the listed specialised areas.
Name the four areas in which the 500-hour component may be acquired, singly or in combination.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Clinical pharmacy, a demonstration project, manufacturing, and analytical or industrial pharmacy (247 CMR 8.01(1)(a)2).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registered pharmacist preceptor shall not directly supervise more than ______ pharmacy interns ______.
Who may directly supervise a Massachusetts pharmacy intern, and does the answer change once the intern has logged most of the required hours?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A registered pharmacist preceptor, which 247 CMR 2.00 defines as a registered pharmacist in good standing who has completed at least one year of the actual practice of pharmacy and whom the Board has approved to supervise and direct the training of pharmacy interns; and no. 247 CMR 8.01(3) states the requirement without any hours trigger, so accumulated experience does not create an authority to work unsupervised.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does direct supervision of a pharmacy intern consist of under 247 CMR 2.00?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Oversight and direction of the intern's professional activities by a Board-approved registered pharmacist preceptor, including directly reviewing the intern's work.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: May a pharmacy intern supervise pharmacy technicians, and on what condition?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Yes, under 247 CMR 8.01(15), but only while the intern is itself acting under the direct supervision of a registered preceptor.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An intern must give the Board written notice of withdrawal from an approved college or school of pharmacy or PharmD program within ______, and the duty sits on ______.
True or false: graduating from an approved college or school of pharmacy ends a pharmacy intern's capacity to act as a pharmacy intern.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 247 CMR 8.01(10) a pharmacy intern who has graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy may continue to act in the capacity of pharmacy intern until becoming licensed as a pharmacist.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a graduate of a non-approved school of pharmacy needs FPGEC certification before a Massachusetts internship may commence.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 247 CMR 8.01(7) requires NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE, issued within the preceding year, with a copy provided to the Board; an FPGEC certification is a different credential and is not what 8.01(7) asks for.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: accepting a pharmacy residency in Massachusetts is itself authority for a PharmD graduate to practise there.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 247 CMR 8.01(8) the graduate must apply for and obtain a pharmacy intern license until obtaining a Massachusetts pharmacist license, and while enrolled must hold either a Massachusetts pharmacist license or a Massachusetts intern license with pharmacist supervision.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A Massachusetts school of pharmacy tells students that its new clinical pharmacy program will count toward the internship. Who actually decides, and on what?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Board decides, on the written description of the project or program that 247 CMR 8.01(12) requires the school to submit.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an intern found to have violated state regulations during the internship faces sanctions on the intern license and nothing more.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 247 CMR 8.01(17) the intern may be prohibited from taking the examination for licensure, in addition to other sanctions imposed by the Board. The limit to keep in view is 247 CMR 8.08: no person shall be denied initial licensure or renewal due to a sanction arising from providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive or gender-affirming health care services that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice there.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does the Board require before granting credit for internship experience acquired in another jurisdiction?
retrieval_prompts.answer: An affidavit or certificate of approval issued by that jurisdiction, presented to the Board and indicating that the experience was duly approved there (247 CMR 8.01(11)).

quick_review.text: The first internship pathway is at least 1500 hours of Board-approved experience, split into at least 1000 hours in a pharmacy or pharmacy-related setting approved by the Board and at least 500 hours in clinical pharmacy, a demonstration project, manufacturing, or analytical or industrial pharmacy.
The alternative pathway is at least 1500 intern hours acquired through experiential pharmacy education, where the student is a graduate of an ACPE-accredited college or university.
No more than 12 hours of pharmacy internship credit may be received per day.

Separately, a pharmacy intern may not practice in a pharmacy for more than 12 hours in a 24 hour period without completing an eight consecutive hour rest period before resuming work, unless an extenuating circumstance requires it in the best interest of the patient and the excess is minimized and documented by the licensee.

A pharmacy intern shall work under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor: a registered pharmacist in good standing with at least one year of actual practice whom the Board has approved, whose direct supervision includes directly reviewing the intern's work.
A registered pharmacist preceptor shall not directly supervise more than two pharmacy interns at one time, and an intern acting under direct preceptor supervision may supervise pharmacy technicians.

A graduate of a non-approved college or school of pharmacy must hold NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE issued within the preceding year, and provide a copy to the Board, before commencing a Massachusetts internship.

A PharmD graduate who has accepted a Massachusetts residency must obtain a pharmacy intern license until licensed as a pharmacist, and while enrolled must hold either a Massachusetts pharmacist license or a Massachusetts intern license with pharmacist supervision.

A school submits a written description of each demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program for which internship credit is desired, and the Board determines whether participation may be credited; the Board also issues the Summary of Objectives and Procedures for Pharmacy Internship and preceptor and intern guidelines.

An intern must give the Board written notification within 14 days of withdrawing from an approved college or school of pharmacy or PharmD program, while graduation from an approved school leaves the intern capacity intact until licensure.

An intern found to have engaged in conduct in violation of federal and/or state laws and/or regulations may be prohibited from taking the examination for licensure, in addition to other sanctions imposed by the Board.

Under 247 CMR 8.08 no person shall be denied initial licensure or renewal due to a complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from reproductive or gender-affirming health care services that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice there.

decision_logic.condition: An intern's shift is scheduled, or is running, past 12 hours of practice in a 24-hour period.
decision_logic.action: Apply 247 CMR 9.01(17) before any question of credit: more than 12 hours is permitted only in an extenuating circumstance, in the best interest of the patient, with the excess minimized and documented by the licensee, and the intern must complete an eight consecutive hour rest period before resuming work in a pharmacy. A routinely scheduled long shift has no extenuating circumstance behind it.

decision_logic.condition: A day's internship hours are being recorded.
decision_logic.action: Credit no more than 12 hours for that day under 247 CMR 8.01(4), however long the intern was present and whatever the reason; time worked beyond 12 hours, even time worked lawfully under the extenuating-circumstance exception in 247 CMR 9.01(17), is not internship credit.

decision_logic.condition: An intern is scheduled to work.
decision_logic.action: Confirm a registered pharmacist preceptor is providing direct supervision, whatever the intern's accumulated hours, because 247 CMR 8.01(3) attaches no hours threshold.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist is proposed as the preceptor who will directly supervise an intern.
decision_logic.action: Check the 247 CMR 2.00 definition: a registered pharmacist in good standing, with at least one year of the actual practice of pharmacy, whom the Board has approved to supervise and direct the training of pharmacy interns. Then confirm the supervision will be direct, meaning the preceptor oversees and directs the intern's professional activities and directly reviews the intern's work.

decision_logic.condition: A preceptor is asked to take on another intern.
decision_logic.action: Count the interns that preceptor is already directly supervising; stop at two under 247 CMR 8.01(16), and do not treat headroom in the general support-personnel ratio as authority for a third.

decision_logic.condition: A candidate graduated from a non-approved college or school of pharmacy and wants to begin an internship.
decision_logic.action: Before the internship commences, verify NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE issued within the preceding year and confirm a copy has gone to the Board with any other required documentation.

decision_logic.condition: A PharmD graduate is starting a Massachusetts residency without a pharmacist license.
decision_logic.action: Require a Massachusetts pharmacy intern license and pharmacist supervision; the residency appointment itself is not the credential.

decision_logic.condition: An intern leaves an approved college or school of pharmacy or a PharmD program.
decision_logic.action: Distinguish withdrawal from graduation. Withdrawal starts a 14-day clock for the intern's own written notification to the Board; graduation does not, and the intern capacity continues until licensure.

decision_logic.condition: A school or a candidate asserts that particular activity counts toward the internship.
decision_logic.action: Ask who determined that. A school demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program is creditable only on the Board's determination following the school's written description, and out-of-state experience only on an affidavit or certificate of approval presented to the Board.

decision_logic.condition: An intern is found to have engaged in conduct violating federal or state law or regulation.
decision_logic.action: Advise that the Board may prohibit the intern from taking the licensure examination in addition to other sanctions, and that preceptor and intern reporting on the Board's form continues to be owed in a timely manner throughout the internship. If the sanction arose from providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive or gender-affirming health care services that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice there, 247 CMR 8.08 bars denying initial licensure or renewal because of it.

exceptions.text: The 1000-hour and 500-hour composition belongs to the first pathway only. The alternative in 247 CMR 8.01(1)(b), at least 1500 intern hours acquired through experiential pharmacy education for a graduate of an ACPE-accredited college or university, states no internal split.

Internship experience acquired outside Massachusetts is not excluded. Under 247 CMR 8.01(11) the Board may grant credit for it where an affidavit or certificate of approval from the jurisdiction where it was acquired is presented to the Board.

A PharmD graduate enrolled in a Massachusetts residency who already holds a Massachusetts pharmacist license does not need the intern license route in 247 CMR 8.01(8); holding the pharmacist license is the alternative the provision offers.

Graduation is the case where nothing further is required. 247 CMR 8.01(10) lets a pharmacy intern who has graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy continue to act in the capacity of pharmacy intern until becoming licensed as a pharmacist, in contrast to the withdrawal case.

The practice limit in 247 CMR 9.01(17) yields to an extenuating circumstance: the intern may exceed 12 hours in order to act in the best interest of the patient, provided the time in excess of 12 hours is minimized and the licensee documents the extenuating circumstance. The exception reaches the practice limit only; it does not lift the 12-hour credit ceiling in 247 CMR 8.01(4).

247 CMR 8.08 qualifies the licensure consequences of conduct: no person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline, or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, so long as the services provided would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts.

timing_deadlines.event: Withdrawal from an approved college or school of pharmacy or a PharmD program
timing_deadlines.consequence: The intern personally owes written notification to the Board; the duty does not pass to the school or the employer and does not wait on a decision to reapply.

timing_deadlines.event: NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE, held by a graduate of a non-approved school
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Issued within the year preceding the commencement of the internship
timing_deadlines.consequence: An older authorization does not satisfy 247 CMR 8.01(7) and the internship may not commence on it.

timing_deadlines.event: A single day of internship activity
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No more than 12 hours of internship credit per day
timing_deadlines.consequence: Credit for the day stops at 12 hours. Whether any time beyond 12 hours could be worked at all is a separate question under 247 CMR 9.01(17), and time worked under its extenuating-circumstance exception is still not credited beyond 12 hours.

timing_deadlines.event: Practice by a pharmacy intern in a pharmacy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No more than 12 hours in a 24 hour period, then an eight consecutive hour rest period before resuming work in a pharmacy
timing_deadlines.consequence: Exceeding 12 hours is permitted only in an extenuating circumstance, to act in the best interest of the patient, with the excess minimized and the circumstance documented by the licensee.

timing_deadlines.event: The course of the pharmacy internship
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Throughout the internship, in a timely manner
timing_deadlines.consequence: Preceptors and pharmacy interns submit, on a form provided by the Board, such information regarding the internship as the Board may require.

timing_deadlines.event: A pharmacy intern's graduation from an approved college or school of pharmacy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Until the graduate becomes licensed as a pharmacist
timing_deadlines.consequence: The intern may continue to act in the capacity of pharmacy intern.

timing_deadlines.event: Acceptance of a residency in Massachusetts by a PharmD graduate of an approved school
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Until a Massachusetts pharmacist license is obtained
timing_deadlines.consequence: The graduate must apply for and obtain a pharmacy intern license.

forms_records.text: During the course of the internship, preceptors and pharmacy interns submit information about the internship on a form provided by the Board, in a timely manner, as the Board requires.
Written notification of withdrawal from an approved college or school of pharmacy or PharmD program goes to the Board from the intern, within 14 days.
A graduate of a non-approved college or school of pharmacy provides the Board with a copy of the NABP FPGEE authorization, along with any other documentation the Board requires.
Out-of-state internship experience is documented to the Board by an affidavit or certificate of approval issued by the jurisdiction where the experience was acquired.

A Massachusetts approved college or school of pharmacy files a written description of each demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program for which internship credit is desired, and the Board issues the Summary of Objectives and Procedures for Pharmacy Internship together with guidelines for registered pharmacist preceptors and pharmacy interns.
A PharmD graduate who has accepted a Massachusetts residency applies for a pharmacy intern license and holds it until a Massachusetts pharmacist license is obtained.
Where an extenuating circumstance takes a pharmacy intern past 12 hours of practice in a 24 hour period, the licensee documents the extenuating circumstance under 247 CMR 9.01(17).

role_duties.duty: Hold the qualifications 247 CMR 2.00 attaches to the title (a registered pharmacist in good standing, at least one year of actual practice, Board approval) and provide the direct supervision on which the intern's authority to work rests, by overseeing and directing the intern's professional activities and directly reviewing the intern's work; 247 CMR 8.01(3) names this role specifically and admits no substitute.
Directly supervise no more than two pharmacy interns at one time, counting interns rather than total support personnel.
During the course of the internship, submit in a timely manner and on a Board form such information regarding the internship as the Board may require.
Work only under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor, and record no more than 12 hours of internship credit for any one day.

Practise in a pharmacy no more than 12 hours in a 24 hour period without completing an eight consecutive hour rest period before resuming work, and where an extenuating circumstance requires more in the best interest of the patient, keep the excess to a minimum and document the circumstance.
May supervise pharmacy technicians, but only while acting under the direct supervision of a registered preceptor.
Provide the Board with written notification within 14 days of withdrawing from an approved college or school of pharmacy or a PharmD program, personally.

Submit required internship information on the Board's form in a timely manner, and understand that conduct violating federal or state law or regulation may cost access to the licensure examination in addition to other sanctions.

role_duties.role: PharmD graduate enrolled in a Massachusetts residency
role_duties.duty: Hold either a Massachusetts pharmacist license or a Massachusetts pharmacy intern license with pharmacist supervision; the residency appointment is not itself a credential.

role_duties.role: Graduate of a non-approved college or school of pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Obtain NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE issued within the preceding year, and provide a copy to the Board with any other required documentation, before the internship commences.

role_duties.role: Massachusetts approved college or school of pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Submit to the Board a written description of each demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program for which internship credit is desired, and leave the creditability determination to the Board.

Determine whether participation in a submitted project or program is creditable, issue the Summary of Objectives and Procedures for Pharmacy Internship and preceptor and intern guidelines, and decide whether out-of-state experience is credited on the documentation presented.

common_traps.text: Treating the 1500 hours as one undivided number. On the first pathway the 1000-hour and 500-hour components are part of the requirement, and a record that reaches 1500 hours in the wrong mix does not satisfy 247 CMR 8.01(1)(a).
Reading an hours figure as a licensure milestone. Neither 500 nor 1000 nor 1400 hours unlocks independent practice; the direct-supervision requirement in 247 CMR 8.01(3) has no hours trigger at all.

Treating a long intern shift as a question about the log. Under 247 CMR 9.01(17) a pharmacy intern may not practice in a pharmacy for more than 12 hours in a 24 hour period without an eight consecutive hour rest period, save a documented extenuating circumstance with the excess minimized; and whatever the reason for a longer day, 247 CMR 8.01(4) still credits no more than 12 hours.
Answering a preceptor-load question from the general support-personnel ratio. The two-intern cap in 247 CMR 8.01(16) is a separate limit and is not relieved by headroom under 247 CMR 8.06(3).

Treating any pharmacist on duty as a preceptor. 247 CMR 2.00 requires a registered pharmacist in good standing with at least one year of actual practice whom the Board has approved, and direct supervision includes directly reviewing the intern's work.
Assuming that an intern supervising pharmacy technicians has stepped outside supervision. 247 CMR 8.01(15) makes the intern's own direct supervision the condition of that authority.

Confusing the pre-internship gate with the examination credential. 247 CMR 8.01(7) asks for NABP authorization to sit for the FPGEE, issued within the preceding year and copied to the Board; an FPGEC certification is a different document and does not answer that provision.

Treating a residency appointment as authority to practise. 247 CMR 8.01(8) requires the PharmD graduate to hold a Massachusetts pharmacist license, or a Massachusetts intern license with pharmacist supervision, regardless of the appointment.

Running graduation and withdrawal together. Graduation from an approved school leaves the intern capacity intact and triggers no filing; withdrawal starts a 14-day written notification duty that sits on the intern rather than on the school.

Reading 247 CMR 8.01(10) as making every graduate an intern. It lets a pharmacy intern who has graduated continue in that capacity until licensed; it does not confer intern status on a graduate who never held it.
Letting the school be the decision-maker on internship credit. Under 247 CMR 8.01(12) the school submits a written description and the Board determines whether participation may be credited.

Reading the examination prohibition in 247 CMR 8.01(17) as an alternative to other sanctions, or as automatic. The provision says the intern may be prohibited from taking the examination in addition to other sanctions imposed by the Board.
